records.description: Potters Industries, LLC manufactures glass beads, microspheres and engineered materials used in road and airfield markings and specialized industrial applications. The company is headquartered in Malvern, Pennsylvania and operates a broad manufacturing and logistics network across North America and Europe, with additional presence in South America and Asia. A Macquarie Asset Management-led consortium acquired control in December 2025 through the Macquarie Strategic Opportunities Fund infrastructure-adjacent private-equity strategy. UniSuper publicly discloses an approximately 30% interest and Partners Capital is a named co-investor; the remaining consortium split is not publicly disclosed.

records.description: TraPac, LLC operates marine container terminals in Los Angeles and Oakland serving ocean carriers, truckers, rail providers and cargo owners moving containerized freight through the U.S. West Coast. The capital-intensive platform includes berth access, cranes, yard and gate systems and intermodal rail connectivity. Ocean Network Express acquired 51% on November 2, 2023 and Macquarie Infrastructure Partners VI acquired 49% on November 1, 2023; the owners exercise joint control. Mitsui O.S.K. Lines and Brookfield Asset Management are former owners. TraPac Jacksonville transferred separately to Ceres in 2022 and is excluded from this platform boundary.

records.description: Yusen Terminals LLC operates a marine container terminal at the Port of Los Angeles on Terminal Island. Its infrastructure includes berths, cargo-handling cranes, storage yards, gate systems, on-dock rail and shore-power facilities serving container lines and North American import and export supply chains. Ocean Network Express acquired NYK's 51% interest in 2023 and subsequently became the terminal's sole owner after Macquarie Infrastructure Partners III sold its separate 49% interest for US$550 million. The exact closing date and buyer vehicle for Macquarie's later sale were not publicly disclosed.

records.description: TowerPoint Infrastructure Partners is a U.S. wireless-infrastructure platform that acquires, owns, and manages towers, easements, rooftops, and related telecom real estate for wireless carriers and other network operators. The business traces its operating roots to 2007 and reported more than 900 assets across 49 states and approximately $1.5 billion invested by year-end 2025. Meritage Group and Ullico Infrastructure Fund entered through the December 2024 recapitalization, and Munich Re later acquired a 15.0% interest through MEAG-managed MR Highland. TowerPoint Capital manages the platform; its direct equity participation is not publicly disclosed and is not recorded as ownership.

records.description: Centre de recherche du CHUM (CRCHUM) is a long-term social-infrastructure public-private partnership in Montréal that houses health-research, learning, simulation, and administrative functions for the Centre hospitalier de l'Université de Montréal. The approximately 68,000-square-meter facility operates under the Accès Recherche Montréal project company and an availability-payment DBFM structure extending to September 2043. Axium Infrastructure and Meridiam remain the current infrastructure owners; QIC held a 19.6% interest from 2012 until selling it to Meridiam in September 2023. The separate main CHUM hospital PPP is not part of this record.

records.description: Altán Redes operates Red Compartida, Mexico's national wholesale mobile network. The platform provides 4.5G LTE wholesale capacity to mobile network operators, MVNOs, enterprises, and public-sector users and reports coverage above 94% of Mexico's population. Morgan Stanley Infrastructure Partners remains the majority owner through the Marapendi and North Haven Infrastructure Partners II chain with 51.37% of Altán's capital. Comisión Federal de Electricidad acquired the remaining 48.63% through trust F/1320 in 2025. Separate governance rights held by Mexican development banks arise from restructuring debt and are not recorded as equity ownership.

records.description: Mercury Fiber is a facilities-based rural broadband platform that develops and operates fiber-to-the-premises and fixed-wireless networks across underserved communities in the central United States. Northleaf completed a controlling investment on October 31, 2022 through NCP Mercury AIV LP and Mercury TopCo, LLC. Mercury's pre-closing owner retained minority rollover equity, but the parties' current exact economic percentages and Northleaf fund allocation are not publicly disclosed.

records.description: Millennium Parking Garages, LLC operates the long-term concession for four underground parking garages beneath Millennium, Grant and Maggie Daley Parks in downtown Chicago. The system serves commuters, residents, visitors and event traffic through approximately 9,176 spaces across 3.8 million square feet. Northleaf and AMP Capital acquired the concession on May 18, 2016. Northleaf continues to hold an inferred 50% interest, while InfraBridge manages the other 50% through Global Infrastructure Fund I following its February 2, 2023 succession to AMP Capital's infrastructure-equity management business. No subsequent sale or signed ownership transfer was identified through September 1, 2026.

records.description: Pocahontas Parkway Operations, LLC operates the long-term tolled-road concession south of Richmond, Virginia. The manager-level platform includes the 8.8-mile Pocahontas Parkway, its James River crossing, tolling systems and the 1.58-mile Richmond Airport Connector; bridges, ramps, plazas and financing vehicles remain components rather than separate PortCos. Globalvia completed its acquisition on December 20, 2016 and currently reports a 68.14% stake. Northleaf joined as a direct co-investor in 2017 and remains active; its exact ownership percentage is not publicly disclosed. No later equity sale or signed pending transfer was identified through September 1, 2026.

records.description: Ascension FBO Network is an 11-location U.S. fixed-base operator platform that provides aircraft fueling, hangaring, ground handling and passenger and crew services for business and general aviation, with selected airline and military support. The platform was formed as Hawthorne Global Aviation Services in 2011 and adopted the Ascension commercial brand during 2025. NOVA Infrastructure and Wafra completed their joint acquisition on March 15, 2022 through Hawthorne FBO Acquisition Co.; exact economic percentages and Wafra's fund allocation are not publicly disclosed. Individual airport locations, leases and add-on businesses remain beneath the single manager-level platform.
